spec: Revision/SPEC.md sections 1-6: scope of the non-triviality, quantisation and energy statements
independence: no code shared with Revision/theory/wolfram/verify_scope.wls or with the other Revision verifiers; own coefficient ring, own vielbein, connection and Riemann computation
metric: the corrected metric of 2026-10-16: diag(e^(-2 a4) b4 cot^2 z, e^(2 a4) (x3), -1, -e^(-2 a4) b4 (sin^2 z)^(1/6) (x3)), z = 6 H x0 real
coordinates: the author's coordinates x0..x7: x0 = the hidden, space-like direction, z = 6 H x0 real (-infinity < z < infinity); x1, x2, x3 = 3-space; x4 = time; x5, x6, x7 = the exponentially deflating extra times

checks.name: zero_test_controls
checks.detail: the exact zero test of this checker (every real z): c^2 + sv^2 - 1, w^12 - sv^2, sgn^2 - 1 and ch^2 - sh^2 - 1 are zero; w^6 - sv and w^6 + sv (|sin z| -+ sin z) and sgn - 1 are not (no sign of sin z is assumed); the x0 derivatives of the ring respect w^12 = sv^2

checks.name: boosted_frame_reproduces_metric
checks.detail: the frame boosted in the (x4, x0) plane, e'^(x4) = cosh b e^(x4) + sinh b e^(x0), e'^(x0) = sinh b e^(x4) + cosh b e^(x0) (other e'^(a) = e^(a), b = b(x4) = beta x4 + b0), with e^(a) the diagonal vielbein (f = (e^-a4 b4^(1/2) cot z, e^a4 [x3], 1, e^-a4 b4^(1/2) (sin^2 z)^(1/12) [x3]), order x0..x7): eta_ab e'^a_mu e'^b_nu equals the corrected metric for all 64 (mu, nu) and every real z, and e' E' = 1

checks.name: boosted_frame_canonical_connection
checks.detail: canonical spin connection of the boosted frame, omega_mu^a_b = e'^a_nu (d_mu e'_b^nu + Gamma^nu_mu,lam e'_b^lam): the vielbein postulate holds for all 512 (a, mu, nu) (0 failures) and omega_mu ab = eta_ac omega_mu^c_b is antisymmetric in a, b for every mu (exact, symbolic a4, b4, H, beta, every real z)

checks.name: boosted_frame_gammaOmega_formula
checks.detail: in the boosted frame gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = (cg - beta/2) (cosh b gamma^(x0) - sinh b gamma^(x4)) + vg (cosh b gamma^(x4) - sinh b gamma^(x0)), cg = (3/2) H e^a4 b4^(-1/2), vg = b4'/b4 - a4'/2, exactly for every a4(x4), b4(x4), H > 0, rapidity rate beta and every real z; at b = 0 this is the value cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4) of the diagonal frame. Its coefficients satisfy cosh b c4 + sinh b c0 = vg for every beta, so no such boost makes gamma'^mu Omega'_mu vanish unless b4'/b4 = a4'/2

checks.name: boosted_frame_removes_only_the_H_term
checks.detail: with a rapidity b(x4) of rate b' = 2 cg = 3 H e^a4 b4^(-1/2) the term gamma'^mu D'_mu - gamma'^mu d_mu = gamma'^mu Omega'_mu is vg (cosh b gamma^(x4) - sinh b gamma^(x0)) for every H > 0, a4(x4), b4(x4) (exact): its cg part belongs to the diagonal vielbein and is not a frame-independent part of the field equation, while the vg part is not removed by any boost in this plane (previous check). Omega'_mu itself is nonzero for mu = x0, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, as it must be where the metric is curved (next check)

checks.name: boosted_frame_curvature_nonzero
checks.detail: in the boosted frame (b' = 2 cg) the spinor curvature F'_x5x0 = d_x5 Omega'_x0 - d_x0 Omega'_x5 + [Omega'_x5, Omega'_x0] is nonzero for general a4, b4: Omega' cannot vanish in this frame, and in no frame where the metric is curved, because its curvature is (1/2) R_ab,mu,nu S^ab; what vanishes in this frame is only the cg part of the contraction gamma'^mu Omega'_mu (the corrected metric is flat for special a4, b4)

checks.name: rescaling_removes_the_connection_term
checks.detail: diagonal frame: gamma^mu Omega_mu = cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4) (control), and for Psi = e^(a4/2) b4^(-1) (sin^2 z)^(-1/8) chi with any 16 component functions chi(x0, ..., x7): gamma^mu D_mu Psi - e^(a4/2) b4^(-1) (sin^2 z)^(-1/8) gamma^mu d_mu chi = (gamma^mu d_mu ln W + gamma^mu Omega_mu) W chi = 0 exactly, W the factor (the x0 terms: e^a4 b4^(-1/2) tan z (-(3/2) H cot z) + cg = 0; the x4 terms: a4'/2 - b4'/b4 + vg = 0; the operator is first order, so this matrix identity is the identity for every chi). In the variables chi the field equation has no spin-connection term: gamma^mu d_mu chi = (m + U'(S)) chi

checks.name: rescaled_equation_quadratic_potential
checks.detail: with U = (lambda/2) S^2 and Psi = e^(a4/2) b4^(-1) (sin^2 z)^(-1/8) chi: S[Psi] = Psi^dagger C Psi = e^a4 b4^(-2) |sin z|^(-1/2) S[chi], so the rescaled equation is gamma^mu d_mu chi = (m + lambda e^a4 S[chi]/(b4^2 |sin z|^(1/2))) chi exactly: for U = 0 the spin-connection term is removed completely, for U != 0 it becomes an x0- and x4-dependent coupling. The exact U = 0 family (i-b) of the theory record (al = -1/4) is the same statement: its coefficient (3/2) H (4 al + 1) e^a4 b4^(-1/2) of gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) vanishes

checks.name: gammaOmega_sees_the_hidden_block
checks.detail: diagonal frame: gamma^mu Omega_mu = (3/2) H e^a4 b4^(-1/2) gamma^(x0) + (b4'/b4 - a4'/2) gamma^(x4) contains a4 (e^a4 and a4'): its gamma^(x0) coefficient is (3/2) H times the inverse scale factor of the hidden block (unlike the metric of 2026-10-14, whose term 3 H gamma^(x0) + (3/4)(b4'/b4) gamma^(x4) contained no a4); own Riemann computation from the Christoffel symbols, compared exactly (ring: b4''/b4 = B2 + B1^2): R^x4_x4 = 7 a4'^2 - a4'' - 4 a4' b4'/b4 + 2 b4''/b4 - (b4'/b4)^2, R^x1_x1 = -a4'^2 + a4'' + 2 a4' b4'/b4, R^x0_x0 = R^x5_x5 = -3 Cb + a4'^2 - a4'' - (5/2) a4' b4'/b4 + (1/2) b4''/b4 + (1/2)(b4'/b4)^2, Cb = H^2 e^(2 a4)/b4

checks.name: connection_free_lagrangian_same_equations
checks.detail: diagonal frame: {gamma^mu, Omega_mu} = 0 for each mu separately, so Psibar {gamma^mu, Omega_mu} Psi = 0 and the canonical spin connection drops out of the symmetrised Lagrangian: L(Omega) = L(Omega = 0) identically, and its Euler-Lagrange equations equal those of the connection-free symmetric Lagrangian, gamma^mu d_mu Psi + (1/(2 sqrt|g|)) d_mu(sqrt|g| gamma^mu) Psi = (m + U') Psi; the matrix identity (1/(2 sqrt|g|)) d_mu(sqrt|g| gamma^mu) = gamma^mu Omega_mu = cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4) is recomputed here (sqrt|g| = sgn e^-a4 b4^2 cot z (sin^2 z)^(1/4)): the surviving term is the half-density term

checks.name: spin_connection_in_the_energy_momentum_tensor
checks.detail: diagonal frame, homogeneous configuration Phi = Phi(x4): the connection part of K^x4_x1 = (1/2)(Phibar gamma^x4 D_x1 Phi - D_x1 Phibar gamma^x4 Phi) is (1/2) Phibar {gamma^x4, Omega_x1} Phi = 0 (3-space does not depend on x0), while that of K^x4_x5 is (1/2) Phibar {gamma^x4, Omega_x5} Phi = (1/2) H (sin^2 z)^(1/12) Phibar gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) gamma^(x5) Phi (the a4', b4' part cancels exactly); C gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) gamma^(x5) != 0, so the canonical spin connection contributes to the off-diagonal energy-momentum tensor through the extra times although it drops out of the Lagrangian

checks.name: good_sector_hermiticity_up_to_the_brane_flux
checks.detail: curved good-sector mode operator at k = 0, h = -i m gamma^(x4) + i gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) e^a4 b4^(-1/2) (tan z d_x0 + (3/2) H) - i vg (i d_x4 Psi = h Psi for U = 0): sqrt|g| [u^dagger (h v) - (h u)^dagger v] = d_x0(sgn b4^(3/2) (sin^2 z)^(1/4) u^dagger M0 v) - i (d_x4 sqrt|g|) u^dagger v, M0 = i gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0), for all u(x0), v(x0) and every real z (matrix identities: sqrt|g| (coefficient of d_x0) = sgn b4^(3/2) (sin^2 z)^(1/4) M0, sqrt|g| (A - A^dagger) = (d_x0 sgn b4^(3/2) (sin^2 z)^(1/4)) M0 - i (d_x4 sqrt|g|) for the algebraic part A, coefficient of d_x0 anti-Hermitian; d_x4 sqrt|g| = 2 vg sqrt|g|, so the anti-Hermitian term -i vg compensates the x4 dependence of the measure). The inner product int sqrt|g| u^dagger v dx0 is therefore conserved only up to the boundary term [b4^(3/2) (sin^2 z)^(1/4) u^dagger M0 v]: it vanishes where sin z = 0 but not at the degenerate points z = pi/2 + n pi of g00 (|sin z| = 1), e.g. u = v with gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) u = u gives u^dagger M0 u = 2*I (|u|^2 = 2); conservation and Krein self-adjointness need boundary conditions there

checks.name: good_sector_x0_independent_modes_without_boundary_condition
checks.detail: on x0-independent good-sector functions (k = 0; finite norm on each interval between the degenerate points, int_0^(pi/(12 H)) cot(6 H x0) sin(6 H x0)^(1/2) dx0 = 1/(3*H)) the curved mode operator acts on Psi as A - i vg, so Psi = e^(a4/2) b4^(-1) chi with i d4 chi = A chi (verified as a matrix identity), A = -i m gamma^(x4) + i cg gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0), which is not Hermitian, and A^2 = (m^2 - cg^2) I16 exactly, cg = (3/2) H e^a4 b4^(-1/2): wherever m^2 < cg^2 the instantaneous frequencies of chi are imaginary. On the record's history a4 = H x4, b4 = e^(4 H x4/3), cg = (3/2) H e^(H x4/3) grows, so every mass falls below it at late x4: without a boundary condition at the degenerate points the good sector contains growing x0-independent modes

checks.name: extra_time_growth_rates_unbounded
checks.detail: flat 4+4 space (or frozen coefficients), plane waves e^(i k.x - i E x4) with h_k = -i m gamma^(x4) - gamma^(x4) sum_a k_a gamma^(a): h_k^2 = (k0**2 + k1**2 + k2**2 + k3**2 - k5**2 - k6**2 - k7**2 + m**2) I16 exactly; for an extra-time momentum k5 = K the growth rate is Im E = sqrt(K**2 - k0**2 - k1**2 - k2**2 - k3**2 - m**2) for K^2 > m^2 + k0^2 + k1^2 + k2^2 + k3^2, which has no upper bound as K grows: the first-order system is not well posed in Hadamard's sense (no continuous dependence on the data in any Sobolev norm) for data that depend on x5, x6, x7. The slices x4 = const are non-characteristic, but that does not make the Cauchy problem well posed

checks.name: commuting_field_energy_unbounded_below
checks.detail: dirac16complex00 (commuting), flat frame, good sector, U = 0, m = 2, k = (k0, k1, k2, k3) = (4, 1, 2, 0), E = 5: h_k commutes with B; the E = +5 eigenspace has dimension 8 and B restricted to it has inertia (4, 4); for the positive-frequency solutions Phi = c u e^(i(k.x - 5 x4)) (field equation verified) with B u = -u and B u = +u (|u| = 1) the energy density rho = -T^x4_x4 = -sum_(mu != x4) K_mu + m S is -5*cc**2 and 5*cc**2 (cc = |c|), and the charge density Phi^dagger B Phi is -cc**2 and cc**2: the classical energy of dirac16complex00 is unbounded below already for U = 0 in the good sector (positive-frequency modes of negative energy), and its U(1) charge is indefinite (only the local law d_mu(sqrt|g| J^mu) = 0 is proved; the total charge is constant in x4 only if no charge flows through the boundary of the slice x4 = const, which at the degenerate points z = n pi/2 is an ASSUMED no-flux condition) - unlike Dirac's 1928 wave function, whose charge density psi^dagger psi is positive
